summary: The three OOMKills of notification-service are caused by the in-heap TemplateCache added by deployment dep-5402 (v3.8.0) on 2026-03-21T00:00Z, which grows without eviction and steadily consumes heap until the container limit is hit (confidence 0.87, high). The evidence chain is tight: memory was flat ~47.7-48.5% all of 03-20, began ramping within ~1.7h of the deploy, and since then has formed a near-identical saw-tooth at a constant ~2%/hour slope that resets only at each restart, with flat request_rate and zero evictions while cache entries rise monotonically. The reporter's Kafka-replay theory is directly contradicted — the two earlier restarts predate the 18:00Z cfg-2410 retention change by 1-2 days, there is no 18:00Z inflection in memory, broker ingest/replication metrics are flat, and the co-tenant shared-Kafka consumer settlement-service shows no anomaly at all. Consumer lag and delayed emails are downstream symptoms of the restart, not the cause. Residual uncertainty (cache unboundedness inferred, not read from code; email-delay attribution assumed) caps confidence below 0.9 but does not support any competing origin.

ranked_hypotheses.title: In-heap TemplateCache introduced by dep-5402 v3.8.0 grows unbounded, exhausting heap and causing OOMKills
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 2026-03-21 deployment dep-5402 (v3.8.0) added an in-memory ConcurrentHashMap template cache keyed by template+locale+userSegment with no eviction. Heap fills steadily at a constant rate as distinct cache keys accumulate, old-gen pressure triggers full GCs, and the container hits its memory limit and is OOMKilled. Three near-identical saw-tooth cycles follow the deploy. Consumer lag and delayed emails are downstream symptoms of the restart, not the cause.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5402 v3.8.0 adds an in-memory TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment) with no eviction, and no notification-service memory-limit/JVM/batch config change accompanies it.
The memory ramp onsets within the hour after the 2026-03-21T00:00Z deploy: memory_pct is flat at ~47.7-48.5% for all of pre-deploy day 03-20, then climbs in the 03-21T01:40Z bucket (51.77%).

The series becomes a per-restart saw-tooth: climb to ~92.8% by 03-21T20:00Z, reset to ~49% after restart #1; climb to ~94.3% by 03-22T19:50Z, reset to ~52% after restart #2; third climb to 83.0% by 03-23T12:20Z.
Climb rate is constant (~2%/hour) across all three cycles rather than accelerating from any single hour, and the ramp resumes immediately after each restart.

Cache entries grow monotonically with 0 evictions (148500 at 14:30Z -> 188100 at 18:54Z) and heap/GC warnings first appear at each cycle's peak just before each restart (first-seen 03-21T21:37:01Z, then 03-22T20:35:10Z-21:56:37Z), with no heap warnings before 03-21T21:37Z.

Memory continues to ramp through 03-23 (83.28% at 14:00Z to a 98.44% peak at 19:45Z) with NO 18:00Z inflection — 91.67% at 17:25Z, 93.67% at 17:50Z, 93.51% at 18:15Z — so the climb is a continuation of the slope already present, not triggered by the Kafka change.
request_rate is flat all week (mean 140.83 req/s) and does not rise during any cycle, so the recurring ramp is not explained by a traffic increase resuming after each restart.
Container is OOMKilled at 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z, exit code 137, immediately after the memory peak.

Restart counter steps 0->1 (~03-21T22:00Z), 1->2 (~03-22T22:00Z), 2->3 (~03-23T20:00Z) — all three restarts post-date the deploy, matching 'third OOM this week'; each memory reset aligns exactly with a restart step.

Consumer lag was normal (~40-93 messages) all day until the 19:45Z bucket, spiked to avg 6082.94/max 18137.93 coincident with the memory peak, peaked at avg 10696.07 in the 20:00Z bucket, then recovered to ~64 by 20:30Z — lag follows the OOM rather than preceding it.
Email delays (~25 min) are the user-visible consequence of the restart-induced consumer outage rather than of a traffic surge.

assumptions: The cache growth is genuinely unbounded (no size cap / TTL) — inferred from the deploy description, monotonically rising entry count and 0 evictions, not from code inspection.

The 03-21T01:40Z onset is attributable to the deploy rather than a routine daily traffic curve; F35 (flat request_rate) argues against a traffic explanation, but no per-instance day-over-day baseline for a non-deployed day is available.

No producer-side volume/size change occurred — F19-F24 now show zero deployments (order-service, payment-service) and zero config/flag changes on the producers in the window, so this is largely closed.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka cfg-2410 retention reduction / maintenance triggered a consumer replay that flooded notification-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Per the reporter, the 2026-03-23T18:00Z Kafka maintenance (log.retention.ms 7d -> 3d) triggered a replay/rebalance, increasing the delivered backlog to notification-service consumers; the consumer processes the burst with the new cache on the render path, memory balloons and the container is OOMKilled.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2410 reduces log.retention.ms 7d -> 3d on shared Kafka at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z, ~2h20m before the report.
Retention truncation/maintenance would deliver a large catch-up backlog to notification-service.
The replay burst would drive the render path and populate TemplateCache, inflating heap.
Heap warnings and memory ramp would then appear.
OOMKill at 19:59:21Z follows.

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Now ruled out on both timing and direct mechanism evidence. Timing: the memory ramp onsets 03-21T01:40Z after dep-5402 (F31) and restart #1/#2 (03-21T~22:00Z, 03-22T~22:00Z) predate the 03-23T18:00Z change by one and two days (F9, F14); there is no 18:00Z inflection in memory at all (F34). Mechanism, previously only assumed away, is now directly contradicted: broker-side ingest (messages_in_per_s) is flat ~2230-2410 msg/s with no replay burst at 18:00Z or at the OOM window (F28), under_replicated_partitions is exactly 0.0 throughout and kafka cpu_pct flat ~33-37% (F29) — no reassignment or saturation. The other shared-Kafka consumer, settlement-service, shows no anomaly: memory flat ~49.55% mean with no 18:00Z deviation (F25), zero restarts all window (F26), normal consumer_lag (mean 45.1, no spike) (F27), and zero WARN+ logs 17:30-23:59Z (F30). Lag spiked only in notification-service (F10). No rollback of cfg-2410 occurred, but nothing downstream ever changed (F5).

ranked_hypotheses.title: A producer-side change on order-service/payment-service increased message volume or size into the shared topic, inflating notification-service memory
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A change or behaviour shift on the upstream Kafka producers (order-service, payment-service) increased the volume or payload size on the shared topic; notification-service consumes larger/more messages, the render path expands into the unbounded TemplateCache, heap grows and the container OOMKills.

causal_chain.claim: notification-service consumes from shared Kafka produced by order-service and payment-service.
An upstream producer change or volume increase reaches the shared topic.
Larger/more messages expand the render path and TemplateCache, raising heap.
OOMKill and lag spike follow.

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The gap the critic flagged (producer history never retrieved) is now closed and returns nothing: order-service has zero deployments (F19) and zero config/flag changes (F21) over 2026-03-01..03-23; payment-service likewise has zero deployments (F20) and zero config/flag changes (F22). The complete all-service deployment list for the window contains only dep-5402 (notification-service) and dep-5415 (auth-service, unrelated jackson bump) (F23), and the complete config-change list contains only cfg-2410 on Kafka (F24). No producer-side payload-schema/size/volume change record exists anywhere. Additionally, the cache key is template+locale+userSegment, so higher message volume would not create new keys and would not grow the cache unboundedly (F1), and request_rate is flat (F35). The multi-day saw-tooth starting 03-21 also predates any speculative upstream event (F9, F31).

ranked_hypotheses.title: notification-service memory limit was reduced or the service was retuned recently, making it OOM-prone without a traffic change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A memory-limit reduction or JVM/heap tuning change made notification-service OOM-prone, so its normal cache footprint now exceeds the container limit and it restarts.

causal_chain.claim: A memory-limit/JVM/batch setting on notification-service was reduced in the window.
Normal heap usage then exceeds the limit, causing OOMKills.

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No such change exists: F3 and F15 report zero config changes for notification-service over 2026-03-01..03-23, explicitly including no memory-limit, consumer/batch or JVM/heap flag change. F24 confirms the complete all-service config-change list for the window contains exactly one entry (cfg-2410 on Kafka), so no out-of-scope notification-service retune is evidenced either. The observed behaviour is also inconsistent with a static limit change: the pattern is a per-cycle climb at a constant ~2%/hour rate that resets only at restart (F32, F33), i.e. a growing footprint, not a fixed footprint newly exceeding a lowered ceiling.

facts.statement: The only notification-service deployment this week is dep-5402 v3.8.0 on 2026-03-21T00:00Z: 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering', changing 'TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap) keyed by template+locale+userSegment' and 'render path uses cache'; status live, rolled_back_at null.

It is the only change in the window that increases the service's in-process memory footprint; the complete all-service deployment list 2026-03-01..03-23 contains only dep-5402 (notification-service) and dep-5415 (auth-service, jackson bump, unrelated).

notification-service memory_pct was flat at ~47.7-48.5% for the entire pre-deployment day 2026-03-20, then began climbing in the 2026-03-21T01:40Z bucket (avg 51.77), i.e. the ramp onsets within ~1.7h of the 03-21T00:00Z deploy.

The memory series is a per-restart saw-tooth of near-identical cycles with a constant ~2%/hour climb that resets only at each restart, with no external trigger: ~92.8% then reset to ~49% after restart #1; ~94.3% then reset to ~52% after restart #2; a third climb to 83.0% by 2026-03-23T12:20Z.
request_rate is flat all week (mean 140.83, min 115.35, max 172.03 req/s) and does not rise during any memory cycle, so the recurring ramp is not explained by a traffic increase.

Cumulative restart count was 0 through 2026-03-21T20:00Z, then stepped 0->1 (~03-21T22:00Z), 1->2 (~03-22T22:00Z), 2->3 (~03-23T20:00Z), matching the report's third OOM restart; each memory reset aligns exactly with a restart step.

The OOMKill is logged exactly once at 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z with exit code 137, immediately after the memory peak of 98.44% at 19:45Z and a sharp drop to ~46% afterwards; memory had ramped steadily from 83.28% at 14:00Z.

TemplateCache entries grew from 148500 (14:30Z) to 188100 (18:54Z) with 0 evictions, and heap/GC warnings ('heap usage 5% over 90 (old gen), full GC took 4152ms') ran from 18:34:46Z to 19:49:28Z — consistent with in-process heap/cache build-up driving the OOM.

Heap/GC warnings first appear at 2026-03-21T21:37:01Z and then 2026-03-22T20:35:10Z-21:56:37Z, i.e. only at the top of each cycle just before each restart, with no heap/GC warnings on 2026-03-20 or before 2026-03-21T21:37Z.

Consumer lag was normal (~40-93 messages) until the 19:45Z bucket, spiked to avg 6082.94 / max 18137.93, peaked at avg 10696.07 in the 20:00Z bucket, then recovered to ~64 by 20:30Z — the lag spike is coincident with the OOM/memory peak, not an earlier independent onset.

The only config change across all services in the window is cfg-2410 on kafka (log.retention.ms 604800000 -> 259200000) at 2026-03-23T18:00Z — 2h20m before the report but 1-2 days after restarts #1 and #2, and after the memory ramp was already underway.
There is no 18:00Z inflection in memory on 03-23: memory_pct rises smoothly through the mark (avg 91.67 at 17:25Z, 93.67 at 17:50Z, 93.51 at 18:15Z).

Kafka broker-side ingest was flat all window — messages_in_per_s ~2230-2410 msg/s with no replay burst at 18:00Z or at the OOM window — and under_replicated_partitions was exactly 0.0 in every bucket with kafka cpu_pct flat ~33-37%, arguing against a broker rebalance/replay mechanism.

The co-tenant shared-Kafka consumer settlement-service showed no deviation: memory flat (mean 49.55%, min 45.4%, max 55.09%) with no 18:00Z or 19:45-20:00Z deviation, zero restarts all window, normal consumer_lag (mean 45.1, no spike), and zero WARN+ logs 17:30-23:59Z.

No producer-side change exists: order-service and payment-service each have zero deployments and zero config/flag changes over 2026-03-01..03-23, and no message-size/volume/payload-schema change record exists anywhere in the window.
No notification-service retune exists: it has zero config changes over 2026-03-01..03-23, specifically no memory-limit, consumer/batch or JVM/heap flag change.
Neither change was rolled back: dep-5402 has rolled_back_at null and no rollback entry appears for cfg-2410.

Historical precedents for the reported lag symptom (HIST-104, HIST-112) are broker/partition rebalancing events, and a search for OOMKilled / unbounded-cache / heap-exhaustion precedents returned no matching incident — so there is no prior OOM precedent corroborating or ruling out this pattern.
Blast radius could not be extended from telemetry: email-provider is external with no metrics and kafka exposes no consumer_lag metric; only notification-service is positively identified as affected.

assumptions: The cache growth is genuinely unbounded (no size cap / TTL) — inferred from the deploy description, monotonically rising entry count and 0 evictions, not from code inspection.

The 2026-03-21T01:40Z onset is attributable to the deploy rather than a routine daily traffic curve; F35 (flat request_rate) argues against a traffic explanation, but no per-instance day-over-day baseline for a non-deployed day is available.
The email delay is a consequence of the restart/lag rather than of an independent traffic or delivery-path surge; no lag/error-rate correlation for the email path was measured.

No producer-side volume/size change occurred — supported by zero deployments and zero config/flag changes on order-service and payment-service and by flat broker ingest, though no direct message-size/schema telemetry exists.
The 15-minute metric bucketing is sufficient resolution to exclude a short-lived 18:00Z event at exactly the cfg-2410 application time.

timeline.event: Baseline day: notification-service memory_pct flat at ~47.7-48.5% for the entire day; no heap/GC warnings logged.

Deployment dep-5402 v3.8.0 goes live on notification-service: 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' (TemplateCache ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment; render path uses cache). Not rolled back.
Memory ramp onsets: memory_pct begins climbing (avg 51.77) in the hour after the deploy, ending the flat ~48% baseline.
First-ever heap/GC warning on notification-service ('heap usage 5% over 90 (old gen), full GC took 4152ms'), at the top of cycle 1.
Restart #1: cumulative restarts step 0->1; memory resets from ~92.8% to ~49% and immediately resumes climbing at the same ~2%/h slope.
dep-5415 auth-service v7.1.4 (jackson bump) deploys; unrelated to notification-service.
Second heap/GC warning burst at the peak of cycle 2 (through 21:56:37Z); memory ~94.3%.
Restart #2: restarts step 1->2; memory resets to ~52% and resumes the identical climb.
Third climb reaches 83.0% with no external trigger; constant ~2%/h slope maintained.
Memory already at 83.28% and continuing to ramp; TemplateCache entries 148500 at 14:30Z.

Kafka cfg-2410 applied (log.retention.ms 7d -> 3d, platform-team 'Kafka maintenance'). No inflection in notification-service memory (91.67 at 17:25Z, 93.67 at 17:50Z, 93.51 at 18:15Z); broker ingest and replication metrics unchanged; settlement-service unaffected.
Heap/GC warnings resume on notification-service and continue sporadically to 19:49:28Z; cache entries reach 188100 by 18:54Z with 0 evictions.
Memory peaks at 98.44%; container hits its limit. Consumer lag bucket spikes to avg 6082.94 / max 18137.93 (from ~40-93 all day).
OOMKill logged exactly once, exit code 137; memory drops sharply to ~46% after the kill.
Restart #3: cumulative restarts step 2->3; consumer lag peaks at avg 10696.07 in this bucket.
Incident INC-004 reported by on-call SRE (OOMKilled restarts, consumer lag spikes, ~25 min email delay), attributed by the reporter to a post-maintenance Kafka replay.
Consumer lag recovers to ~64 messages within ~30 min of the restart, with no change to Kafka or the producers.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back dep-5402 on notification-service (redeploy v3.8.0's predecessor / disable the TemplateCache render path), i.e. revert the exact change id dep-5402 which currently has rolled_back_at null.
recommended_actions.rationale: It is the only change that increased in-process memory footprint, onset of the memory ramp follows it within ~1.7h, and the constant-slope saw-tooth with 0 cache evictions is explained by it; reverting removes the growing heap allocator. Mitigation must be verified by watching memory_pct return to a flat ~48% profile with no heap/GC WARN lines at a cycle peak.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT take Kafka action on account of this incident: leave cfg-2410 in place, do not roll back the retention change, do not force consumer-group reassignment, and do not restart notification-service consumers for 'replay' reasons.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2410 is directly contradicted as the cause: the two earlier OOMs predate it by 1-2 days, there is no 18:00Z memory inflection, broker ingest is flat and under_replicated_partitions is 0.0, and the co-tenant settlement-service shows no anomaly. Acting on Kafka would be an unjustified change to a shared component.

recommended_actions.action: After rollback, confirm the fix over a full cycle window: monitor notification-service memory_pct for at least 24h (memory_pct and restarts metrics) and confirm a flat profile with no climb to the ~92-98% range and no new heap/GC WARN lines at a would-be peak.
recommended_actions.rationale: Each prior cycle climbed at ~2%/h and OOM'd roughly daily; a 24h flat window with zero restart steps is the discriminating verification of the root cause.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument the email path so the 'delayed emails' symptom is measurable rather than assumed: add consumer_lag and error_rate/latency_p99_ms panels plus an end-to-end email-send timestamp, and verify email delay tracks restart events rather than traffic.
recommended_actions.rationale: The Critic flagged that 'email delay is a consequence of the restart, not a traffic surge' is assumed with no lag/error-rate correlation for the email path; request_rate is flat so traffic is unlikely, but the causal hop is unmeasured.

recommended_actions.action: Add a bounded cache policy to TemplateCache: enforce a maximum size and/or TTL (e.g. bounded Caffeine-style cache with eviction metrics) before re-introducing the cache optimization, and add eviction/size metrics with an alert.
recommended_actions.rationale: The unboundedness of the cache is inferred from a monotonically rising entry count with 0 evictions; if the cache optimization is to be kept it must be provably bounded and observable.

recommended_actions.action: Add memory-based guardrails to notification-service: heap/old-gen utilization and full-GC-duration metrics (currently not exposed — heap_old_gen_pct and full_gc_count return not_found) with alerts on sustained old-gen pressure, plus a container memory-usage alert before limit.
recommended_actions.rationale: Heap behavior had to be reconstructed from WARN log lines because no heap/GC time series exists; a numeric old-gen curve and GC-frequency baseline would have surfaced this on 03-21 instead of after the third OOM.

recommended_actions.action: Gate in-memory caching changes behind a canary with a memory-limit soak test, and record code-level cache size-cap/TTL in the deployment record so unbounded-growth risk is reviewable before rollout.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5402 was the only memory-footprint-increasing change in the window and was rolled out fleet-wide with no soak; the deploy description did not state any size cap or TTL.

data_gaps: Deployment/config history for the Kafka producers order-service and payment-service was reportedly unreached by earlier queries; it has since been resolved (zero deployments, zero config/flag changes for both, and the complete all-service change list contains only dep-5402, dep-5415 and cfg-2410), but no direct message-size, payload-schema or per-producer throughput telemetry exists, so producer-side load can only be excluded indirectly.

Kafka exposes no consumer_lag metric and no partition-reassignment/rebalance counter (available: cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions), so a broker-side rebalance event of the HIST-104/HIST-112 type could not be measured directly even though it is indirectly contradicted by flat ingest, 0.0 under-replication and no settlement-service anomaly.

notification-service exposes no heap/GC time series (heap_old_gen_pct and full_gc_count both return not_found); heap/GC behavior was reconstructed only from WARN log lines, so no numeric old-gen curve or GC-frequency baseline exists and the early low-memory part of each ramp has no heap log coverage.
notification-service error_rate and latency_p99_ms were not queried, so the impact of the memory ramp on error rate/latency is unquantified; only the user-reported ~25 min email delay is known.

Kafka WARN/ERROR logs for 14:00-23:59Z were not retrieved, so a Kafka-side maintenance/replay event was not directly corroborated or excluded from Kafka-side logs (it is contradicted by broker metrics and by settlement-service health).
Settlement-service log evidence is limited to a WARN+ query returning total_matched 0 over 17:30-23:59Z; no INFO/DEBUG baseline and no pre-18:00Z window were checked.

Blast radius beyond notification-service is unverified from telemetry: email-provider is external with no metrics and only notification-service was positively identified in the affected data; settlement-service is the one co-tenant that was checked.
cfg-2410's effect at exactly 18:00Z was not diffed at sub-15-minute resolution (data is in 1500s buckets), so a second-level effect coinciding exactly with the change cannot be strictly excluded.

No historical incident matches the OOMKilled + unbounded in-heap cache signature (searches for OOMKilled / memory leak / unbounded cache returned only the unrelated cold-cache HIST-107), so there is no precedent to corroborate the pattern.

No code inspection was performed: cache unboundedness (absence of size cap/TTL) is inferred from the deploy description, monotonically rising entry count and 0 evictions rather than from source or cache configuration.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Verification that dep-5402's TemplateCache has a size cap or TTL and does evict (i.e. the cache is not actually unbounded), which would undercut the stated mechanism even though the timing correlation remains.
A post-rollback observation that memory_pct still climbs at ~2%/h and OOMs again with the cache removed — which would reopen the search for another heap consumer or a container-limit change.

Evidence of a producer-side change on order-service/payment-service that increased message volume or payload size (currently zero deployments and zero config changes exist, so this would require new data).

Direct broker evidence of a replay/rebalance at 18:00Z — e.g. a partition-reassignment counter, a messages_in_per_s surge, under_replicated_partitions > 0, or settlement-service also spiking/restarting at 18:00Z (all currently flat/zero).

Discovery of a notification-service memory-limit, JVM/heap or batching config change recorded outside the queried window/scope, which could make a lowered ceiling rather than a growing footprint the proximate cause.
A day-over-day per-instance baseline showing the same ~2%/h ramp on 03-19/03-20 before the deploy, which would decouple the ramp from dep-5402.

Correlation showing the consumer-lag spike began well before the memory peak (e.g. an onset earlier than ~19:45Z independent of the memory ramp), which would re-elevate an external replay/consumer-side trigger over the cache hypothesis.

Dependency graph: notification-service -> kafka (queue-consume) and -> email-provider (external). kafka is shared=true, owner platform, has_telemetry=true. So the Kafka change is a shared-component change affecting all consumers, not notification-service-specific — blast radius via shared Kafka could touch settlement-service too, but no settlement-service change appeared in the window.

Historical precedents for the reported lag symptom are both broker/partition events, NOT memory/cache: HIST-104 (2025-11-05) 'notification-service lag after Kafka broker rebalance' (consumer lag spike, delayed emails; root cause partition reassignment/rebalancing storm) and HIST-112 (2026-02-03) 'Settlement consumer stalled after partition reassignment' — both attributed to broker maintenance/rebalancing, matching the report's 'Kafka replay' guess on symptoms but not on mechanism.

Searching history specifically for OOMKilled / unbounded-cache / heap-exhaustion precedents returned NO matching incident: the only 'cache' hit was HIST-107 (2025-12-09) 'Cold cache storm after redis failover' (redis-cache, market-data-service; root cause Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica) — a cold/empty cache, the opposite mechanism to a growing in-heap cache, and it does not involve notification-service. So there is no historical precedent for the notification-service OOM/cache-growth pattern to compare against.

settlement-service cumulative restart count was 0 for every 15-min bucket across the whole window 2026-03-23T14:00-23:59Z — no restarts, no OOM-triggered restart on this shared-Kafka consumer.

settlement-service consumer_lag stayed in its normal range all window (mean 45.1 messages, max bucket avg 53.03 at 16:30Z), with no spike at 18:00Z (18:10Z avg 45.41, 18:35Z avg 38.06) and no spike at the notification-service OOM window (19:50Z avg 47.79, 20:15Z avg 44.12) — the lag symptom was confined to notification-service (T1/F10 spiked to avg 6082.94/10696.07), not shared across Kafka consumers.

Kafka broker-side ingest rate was flat across the whole window: messages_in_per_s stayed ~2230-2410 msg/s (min 2045.86, max 2520.49, mean 2295.33), with no replay/backlog surge at 18:00Z (18:10Z avg 2255.4, 18:35Z avg 2223.47) or at the 19:45-20:15Z OOM window (19:50Z avg 2257.72, 20:15Z avg 2254.61) — no broker-side replay burst on the shared Kafka path.

Kafka under_replicated_partitions was exactly 0.0 (avg and max) in every bucket from 14:00Z to 23:35Z, and kafka cpu_pct was flat ~33-37% (mean 34.91%) across the same period — no partition reassignment/under-replication or broker saturation event around the 18:00Z cfg-2410 change or the 20:20Z incident, which argues against a broker-side rebalance/replay mechanism for the observed symptoms.

settlement-service emitted no WARN-or-higher logs at all in 2026-03-23T17:30-23:59Z (total_matched 0, truncated false), so there is no settlement-service-side error/warning evidence near the 18:00Z change or the incident; combined with healthy memory, zero restarts and normal lag, the shared-Kafka path and settlement-service showed no deviation.

notification-service memory_pct is flat at ~47.7-48.5% for the entire pre-deployment day 2026-03-20 (e.g. 48.01 avg at 00:00Z, 47.93 at 23:50Z), then begins climbing in the 2026-03-21T01:40Z bucket (avg 51.77), i.e. the memory ramp onsets in the hour after the 2026-03-21T00:00Z deploy dep-5402 v3.8.0, not at any later trigger.

The memory series is a per-restart saw-tooth of near-identical cycles: climb to ~92.8% by 2026-03-21T20:00Z, reset to ~49% after restart #1 (avg 49.43 at 2026-03-21T23:40Z); climb to ~94.3% by 2026-03-22T19:50Z, reset to ~52% after restart #2 (avg 51.62 at 2026-03-22T23:30Z); climb a third time to 83.0% by 2026-03-23T12:20Z. Each cycle resumes climbing immediately after the restart with no external trigger.

The climb rate is constant (~2%/hour) across all three cycles: from 49.43% (2026-03-21T23:40Z) to 94.29% avg (2026-03-22T19:50Z) and from 51.62% (2026-03-22T23:30Z) to 83.04% avg at 2026-03-23T12:20Z — the same slope each time, so the saw-tooth is uniform rather than accelerating from any single hour.

There is NO 18:00Z inflection on 2026-03-23: in the zoomed 15-min series memory_pct rises smoothly through the 18:00Z mark — avg 91.67 at 17:25Z, avg 93.67 at 17:50Z, avg 93.51 at 18:15Z — with no slope change coinciding with the Kafka cfg-2410 change at 18:00Z; the climb is a continuation of the slope already present since ~14:00Z and earlier.

request_rate is flat all week (mean 140.83, min 115.35, max 172.03 req/s) and does not rise during any memory cycle, so the recurring ramp is not explained by a traffic increase resuming after each restart — the ramp resumes at the same steady request rate.

The restart counter confirms the saw-tooth resets: cumulative restarts stay 0 through 2026-03-21T20:00Z, then step to 1 (~2026-03-21T21:50-23:40Z), 2 (~2026-03-22T21:40-23:30Z) — each reset in memory_pct aligns exactly with a restart step, and the two heap/GC warning bursts (first-seen 2026-03-21T21:37:01Z, then 2026-03-22T20:35:10Z through 21:56:37Z) occur at the peak just before each restart, i.e. at the top of each cycle, with NO heap/GC warnings logged during 2026-03-20 or before 2026-03-21T21:37Z.
